chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Aban and Jameel, from Zurara, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrated to us the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So he called for a cup, took a handful of water, and poured it over his face. Then he wiped his face from both sides together. Then he returned his left hand to the vessel, poured it over his right hand, and wiped its sides. Then he returned his right hand to the vessel, poured it over his left hand, and did just as he had done with the right hand. Then he wiped with what remained in his hand upon his head and his two feet, and he did not return these two to the vessel.
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad perform his ritual ablution (wudu) according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi provides a precise, step-by-step narration of the Prophet’s ablution, emphasizing the Shia practice of wiping the hands sequentially rather than washing them, and performing the foot wipe (masah) without re-immersion. It serves as a key textual evidence for the distinct Shia fiqh of wudu, particularly regarding the method of wiping the feet over the khuffs or skin, contrasting with the Sunni practice of washing. The narration highlights the ritual purity's physical execution as transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing the authority of the Imams in defining prophetic practice.
